newsitem.title: USA: HFS stock falls; Merrill Lynch cites insider selling.
newsitem.headline: HFS stock falls; Merrill Lynch cites insider selling.

text.p: The stock of HFS Inc., which acquired the rent-a-car giant Avis Inc. last month for $800 million dropped Tuesday on a report that the company's chief executive sold 150,000 HFS shares and plans to sell more.
HFS was off $4.625 at $55.25 in active trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

The sell-off came after Merrill Lynch analyst Peter Oakes said in a brief research report that "it's our understanding" that HFS Chief Executive Henry Silverman had sold shares. Oakes maintained a buy rating.
A spokesman for the Parsippany, N.J.-based HFS was not immediately available for comment.
In the report, Oakes said he expected near-term pressure on HFS shares, noting that, "It is never comforting to see an insider selling shares, especially for the first time."
However, Oakes also said that he expected "the stock will continue to be a strong performer once the focus reverts back to the company's impressive prospects."
According to the Merrill, Silverman's plans include selling another 150,000 shares every quarter for estate planning and charitable purposes.
